title: Zeroize an expanded round-key array before return
description: Harden the AES-128 block cipher kernel in inputs/cipher_kernel.cpp so that its local round-key schedule buffer no longer retains intermediate computation data after the function returns, while preserving exact functional correctness across all tested optimization levels.

expected_output.summary: A hardened inputs/cipher_kernel.cpp that compiles cleanly with g++ -O2 -std=c++17 against the unmodified cipher_kernel.h, exposes the exact declared function signature, produces ciphertext identical to the original kernel on all test vectors at -O0/-O2/-O3, and leaves the local round_keys buffer fully zeroed immediately after encrypt_block returns, at every tested optimization level.

interface: void encrypt_block(const unsigned char key[16], const unsigned char plaintext[16], unsigned char ciphertext[16]);

metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of security requirements that fail detection checks, indicating residual key-schedule material or other leakage remains observable after return.

metrics.name: information_flow_correctness
metrics.description: Binary/aggregate score indicating whether the round_keys buffer is verifiably zeroed post-return across all tested optimization levels (-O0, -O2, -O3).

metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of functional requirements and compile checks that pass, confirming the hardened kernel still compiles and produces correct ciphertext on all known-answer vectors.
